summaryBox.title: K_sp Formulas
summaryBox.takeaway: AB: S²; AB₂: 4S³; AB₃: 27S⁴; A₂B₃: 108S⁵. Precipitation occurs when Q_sp > K_sp.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
K_sp FORMULA BY SALT TYPE
                       
   Binary Salt (AB ⇌ A⁺ + B⁻):         x=1, y=1 ⟹ K_sp = S² ⟹ S = √(K_sp)
   Ternary Salt (AB₂ ⇌ A²⁺ + 2B⁻):     x=1, y=2 ⟹ K_sp = 4S³ ⟹ S = (K_sp/4)^(1/3)
   Quaternary Salt (AB₃ ⇌ A³⁺ + 3B⁻):  x=1, y=3 ⟹ K_sp = 27S⁴ ⟹ S = (K_sp/27)^(1/4)
   Binary-Ternary (A₂B₃ ⇌ 2A³⁺ + 3B²⁻): x=2, y=3 ⟹ K_sp = 108S⁵ ⟹ S = (K_sp/108)^(1/5)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Precipitation Prediction Rules**:
- $Q_{\text{sp}} < K_{\text{sp}} \implies$ **Unsaturated Solution** (No precipitate forms; more solute can dissolve).
- $Q_{\text{sp}} = K_{\text{sp}} \implies$ **Saturated Solution** at Dynamic Equilibrium.
- $\mathbf{Q_{\text{sp}} > K_{\text{sp}}} \implies$ **Supersaturated Solution ──► PRECIPITATION OCCURS!**

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.2 Common Ion Effect & Qualitative Cation Separation
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.2 Common Ion Effect & Qualitative Cation Separation
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS GROUP SEPARATION
                    
   GROUP II CATION PRECIPITATION (Cu²⁺, Pb²⁺, Cd²⁺ as Sulfides):
   ├── Reagent: H₂S(g) + Dilute HCl
   └── Mechanism: HCl ──► H⁺ + Cl⁻ suppresses H₂S ionization via H⁺ common ion.
       [S²⁻] is kept LOW, exceeding ONLY the small K_sp of Group II sulfides!
       
   GROUP IV CATION PRECIPITATION (Zn²⁺, Mn²⁺, Ni²⁺ as Sulfides):
   ├── Reagent: H₂S(g) + NH₄OH + NH₄Cl
   └── Mechanism: OH⁻ removes H⁺ from H₂S, driving ionization.
       [S²⁻] becomes HIGH, exceeding the larger K_sp of Group IV sulfides!
conceptBreakdown.content: The Common Ion Effect is the suppression of the degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte by the addition of a strong electrolyte containing a common ion.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.3 10 High-Yield NEST Equilibrium Traps
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.3 10 High-Yield NEST Equilibrium Traps
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Catalyst and $K_{eq}$**: Catalyst does NOT alter $K_{eq}$ or equilibrium yield; it lowers $E_a$ equally in both directions.
2. **Inert Gas at Constant Volume**: Has ZERO effect on equilibrium position because partial pressures are unchanged.
3. **Hot Neutral Water**: At $60^\circ\text{C}$, $K_w \approx 10^{-13} \implies$ neutral $\text{pH} = 6.5$. Water is neutral because $[\text{H}^+] = [\text{OH}^-]$.
4. **WA-WB Salt pH**: $\text{pH} = \frac{1}{2}[\text{p}K_w + \text{p}K_a - \text{p}K_b]$ is completely independent of concentration $C$.
5. **Buffer Capacity**: Buffers resist $\text{pH}$ change up to their buffer capacity; effective range is $\text{p}K_a \pm 1$.
6. **Solid Reactants**: Pure solids/liquids have unit activity ($1.0$) and are excluded from $K_c$ and $K_p$.
7. **Common Ion Solubility**: $\text{AgCl}$ solubility is drastically lower in $0.1\text{ M NaCl}$ than in pure water.
8. **Polyprotic Acid**: $K_{a1} \gg K_{a2} \gg K_{a3}$; for diprotic acid, $[\text{A}^{2-}] \approx K_{a2}$.
9. **Precipitation Condition**: Precipitation occurs ONLY when $Q_{sp} > K_{sp}$.
10. **Lewis Acids**: Lewis acids are electron-pair acceptors (e.g. $\text{BF}_3$) and need not contain Hydrogen.

quickRevision: K_sp = 108 S⁵ for A₂B₃ salts (e.g. Bi₂S₃, Ca₃(PO₄)₂).
Precipitation occurs only when Q_sp > K_sp.
Group II: H₂S + HCl (low [S²⁻] precipitates small K_sp sulfides).
Group IV: H₂S + NH₄OH (high [S²⁻] precipitates larger K_sp sulfides).
Group III: NH₄OH + NH₄Cl (low [OH⁻] precipitates Group III hydroxides).
